title: Faithful to What?
paragraphs: Readers who praise a translation for being faithful rarely say what it is faithful to. The words of the original, its rhythm, its tone, the effect it had on its first audience: these pull in different directions, and loyalty to one is frequently a betrayal of another. The Italian pun that turns the translator into a traitor captures the anxiety but not the structure of the problem.

A more useful framing goes back to Friedrich Schleiermacher, who argued in a lecture of eighteen thirteen that a translator can either leave the writer undisturbed and move the reader towards him, or leave the reader undisturbed and move the writer towards the reader. Much later, the translation scholar Lawrence Venuti recast this as a contrast between foreignizing and domesticating strategies, and argued that English-language publishing had long favoured the second, prizing translations that read as though they had never been translated.

Neither strategy is innocent. A domesticating translation can make a foreign novel feel effortlessly familiar, and in doing so erase precisely the strangeness that made it worth translating. A foreignizing one can preserve that strangeness at the cost of prose so awkward that readers abandon it, which protects the original only in the sense that an unread book cannot be misunderstood.

Vladimir Nabokov pushed something like the foreignizing path about as far as it can go. His English version of Pushkin's Eugene Onegin abandoned rhyme in favour of strict literal sense, supported by a commentary far longer than the poem itself. Admirers saw scholarly honesty; detractors, famously including his longtime friend Edmund Wilson, attacked it harshly. Both responses can be fair at once, since a version may be accurate line by line and lifeless as a whole.

Fidelity, then, is not a single virtue that translations possess in greater or lesser amounts. It is a choice among loyalties, and the most honest translators are perhaps those who tell their readers which loyalty they chose and what it cost.

sources.claim: Schleiermacher 1813 tarihli konferansında çevirmenin ya yazarı rahat bırakıp okuru ona taşıyacağını ya da okuru rahat bırakıp yazarı okura taşıyacağını söyledi; Lawrence Venuti bunu yabancılaştırma/yerlileştirme karşıtlığı olarak yeniden biçimlendirdi ve İngilizce yayıncılığın akıcı, 'görünmez' çevirileri kayırdığını savundu.
Nabokov Puşkin'in Yevgeni Onegin'ini uyaksız, harfi harfine bir çeviriyle ve şiirden çok daha uzun bir şerhle yayımladı; uzun süreli arkadaşı Edmund Wilson çeviriyi sert biçimde eleştirdi.
İtalyanca 'traduttore, traditore' (çevirmen, hain) kelime oyunu çevirinin ihanet sayılabileceği kaygısını dile getirir.
